title: Saturday Science: From A to ZI
tagline: Explore the workings of the brain through hands-on activities and unique scientific resources.
description: Bring kids ages 5–12 to a free monthly Saturday Science session at Columbia’s Jerome L. Greene Science Center. They’ll try hands-on neuroscience activities from BioBus and CUNO, doing simple experiments and demos to see how the brain works. This month’s theme nods to the Zuckerman Institute (“ZI”); registration is required.
description_source: A free monthly event for kids of all ages to explore the workings of the brain through hands-on activities and unique scientific resources. Every month we offer new activities, created by our partners BioBus and CUNO (Columbia University Neuroscience Outreach). Our activities are designed for children ages 5-12, but learners of all ages are invited to join scientists in the Zuckerman Institute’s Education Lab, located at 605 West 129th Street.

description: Explore portraits on view at MoMA and then make your own using collage and drawing in this drop-in family art session at the Cullman Education Building. Kids (5+) can play with symbols, costumes and color to tell a personal story through images. Children will learn simple portrait techniques and how artists use imagery to express identity. Free with advance registration; museum admission and supplies included.
description_source: How do artists tell their stories? Take inspiration from the symbols, costumes, and settings in portraits on view in Frida and Diego: The Last Dream, Ideas of Africa: Portraiture and Political Imagination, and Wifredo Lam: When I Don’t Sleep I Dream. Then use collage and drawing techniques to make a portrait of your own in this drop-in art-making session. Recommended for families with kids ages five and up. This program is free with advance registration and includes admission to the Museum.

title: Vander Ende-Onderdonk House Museum Tours
tagline: Explore New York City's oldest Dutch fieldstone house
description: Bring the family to the Vander Ende-Onderdonk House, a 1709 Dutch fieldstone house in Ridgewood, for weekend guided tours through period rooms and Ridgewood’s story. Kids 5–12 can try a hands-on scavenger hunt, spotting artifacts and solving clues to learn about daily life long ago. Admission is $5; donations welcome.
description_source: The Vander Ende-Onderdonk House, built in 1709, is New York City’s oldest Dutch fieldstone house and operates as a community museum. Open Saturdays and Sundays from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM, it offers guided tours of three floors of period rooms and exhibits detailing 18th- and 19th-century life, including the history of the Vander Ende and Onderdonk families and Ridgewood’s transformation from farmland to industrial neighborhood. Admission is $5 per person. School group visits (Tuesdays/Thursdays) include guided tours and 18th-century craft activities.

title: New England Symphonic Ensemble plays Rutter, Vaughan Williams and More
tagline: A choral evening of classical and contemporary music
description: An evening concert at Carnegie Hall where the New England Symphonic Ensemble and choirs perform choral and orchestral works by Rutter, Vaughan Williams, Mozart, Vivaldi and contemporary composers. It's family-friendly; children under 12 enter free. Kids will hear powerful orchestral sounds, soaring choral singing and pieces in different languages that introduce harmony and musical storytelling. Suitable for all ages.
description_source: Event is Live. Presented by MidAmerica Productions. The New England Symphonic Ensemble performs an evening of contemporary and classic choral music, featuring works by Elaine Hagenberg, Ola Gjeilo, Susan Labarr, Reena Esmail, Daniel Schreiner, and Vaughan Williams. The concert is led by conductors Matthew Chi Lee, Regina McElroy, Nathan Andrew Payant, Jason Strunk, and Steven Zopfi, with participating choirs from around the country. The New England Symphonic Ensemble presents an Easter evening program that spans early Classical and Baroque choral masterworks alongside contemporary sacred music. Under the baton of Terrance Cook-Green, the choir and orchestra perform Mozart’s Missa brevis in D Minor, K. 65, paired with Johnny Edwards’ modern sacred work Risen. The program continues with Vivaldi’s Gloria, led by Bradley D. Vogel, Morten Lauridsen’s Lux Aeterna conducted by Daniel Gordon, and Mozart’s Mass in C Major, K. 317. Join the New England Symphonic Ensemble for an enchanting evening featuring works by Sir John Rutter, including his Requiem and I'll make me a world, as well as Marc-André Bougie's Stabat Mater and the world premiere of Terre Johnson's Te Deum. Conducted by distinguished maestros, this concert promises to be a memorable experience for classical music enthusiasts.
subway: A to 42nd St; N/Q/R to 57th St - 7th Ave
price_summary: Free entry for children under 12; student and senior discounts available at the box office for paid events. Most performances are free.

description: A 30-minute theatre workshop-performance at QED Astoria for kids aged 3–8 and their families, free to attend. Children follow a planter and a seed as the plant grows, watching their relationship shift from curiosity to care and farewell. Short pre- and post-show activities let kids try ideas and share feedback while the piece is in development.
description_source: The Planter plants. Food, drinks, anything. One day, a seed grows into a plant. What follows is a journey exploring their evolving relationship: from getting to know the plant, to witnessing its unique growth, and finally, its departure. This is a theatre piece for 3–8 year olds and their families. This is a work-in-progress performance of a new theatre piece. We’re still in the exploration stage, and workshopping is the best way to gather audience feedback and discover what’s working, and what isn’t.

title: Light, Form and Shadow Workshop with Jim Gingerich
tagline: Discover the foundation of strong drawing and painting by mastering the essential relationship between light, form, and shadow.
description: At Southampton Arts Center, kids ages 5–12 will draw a lit sphere to learn how light shapes form and shadow. They'll start with a circle and an oval for the cast shadow, then use grayscale tones to make their drawings look three-dimensional. Admission $5; Southampton students free.
description_source: Discover the foundation of strong drawing and painting by mastering the essential relationship between light, form, and shadow. In this hands-on class, students will work from a simple sphere placed under a focused light source. As the light casts a clear shadow across the table, you’ll learn how to observe and translate what you see into a convincing, three-dimensional image. Begin by drawing a circle to establish the sphere, followed by an oval to map the cast shadow. From there, using grayscale values, students render the form.

title: NASA’s Mission: Exploring the Universe (A Free, Virtual Lecture)
tagline: A free, virtual lecture about NASA's missions
description: Join a free virtual talk with NASA engineer Dr. Margaret Dominguez about Hubble, Chandra, James Webb and the upcoming Roman Space Telescope. Kids ages 5–18 will hear how these telescopes work, what they’ve discovered, and why engineers solve tricky problems to get those images. Hosted online by Hamptons Observatory; free to register.
description_source: NASA’s missions are at the forefront of transforming our understanding of the universe. Each mission presents a unique challenge, demanding innovative solutions that combine cutting-edge technology with unparalleled reliability. From developing imaging systems on Mars rovers to pioneering laser communication networks that transmit data across millions of kilometers, NASA’s engineers and scientists tackle some of the most complex problems in modern science and engineering. These advancements allow us to observe distant galaxies, study exoplanet atmospheres, and probe the early universe.

title: Living History: The Origins of K-pop Photocards
tagline: Explore the history of K-pop photocards through 19th-century cartes de visites
description: See how today's K-pop photocards grew out of 19th-century cartes de visites at the New York Historical Society. Kids (ages 0–10) can make their own mini CDV, look at historic portrait examples, and take home K-pop–themed freebies. Free with museum admission—great for families who like hands-on crafts and pop-culture stories.
description_source: Did you know that K-pop photocards have a connection with historical figures such as Queen Victoria and Frederick Douglass? People in the mid-1800s got swept up in collecting mini photographs called cartes de visites or CDVs of actors, royalty, activists, musicians, and even their own friends and family members. Join us in celebrating the return of BTS with a look at the long history of photocards. Get your own CDV made and go home with a K-pop themed freebies.

title: Hold On To Your Butts
tagline: A live, shot-for-shot parody of the greatest dinosaur film of all time
description: A live, shot-for-shot parody of a classic dinosaur film performed by two actors and a Foley artist who create all the sound effects onstage. They use cardboard cut-outs, traffic cones and physical comedy to play every character — even the dinosaurs. Best for families with kids 8–12, who’ll laugh, see how Foley works and be invited to use imagination. Tickets at Soho Playhouse; $40 or $80 four-pack with code FAMILY.
description_source: Following its critically acclaimed West End debut, UK tour, and sold-out return to the Edinburgh Fringe, Hold on to Your Butts is heading Off-Broadway for the first time. Performed by just two actors and a Foley artist who creates the sound effects live on stage, the trio reenact each scene and perform every character (including the dinosaurs) in this family-friendly romp. Through comedy, physical theatre and the wildly inventive use of simple props – from cardboard cut-outs, traffic cones and more.

Designed for ages 5–8, kids will follow cocoon-like creatures and take part in a sensory journey about scale and connection. Tickets are choose-what-you-pay (suggested $20) at the Clark Studio Theater.
description_source: This international co-production invites young audiences to discover their relationship with the microscopic, macroscopic, and everything in between! In this original fusion of clowning and theatricality, co-creators Haydeé Boetto and Hélène Ducharme welcome us into a world of cocoons—an astounding universe filled with textures, sounds, and creatures large and small. Weaving sounds of fire, ocean, rain, and thunder, and a visual world inspired by knitted and crocheted yarn, cOsmO will engage young viewers in a sensory exploration of scale and connection.

tagline: Join in a Spring Festival Gala

Food will be donated by local restaurants. The event was originally scheduled for February 22 but was rescheduled due to inclement weather.

tagline: The first major exhibition of Hollywood studio portraiture
description: Face Value at MoMA (Titus and Morita Galleries) brings together over 200 Hollywood studio portraits from 1921–1996 to show how press photography shaped celebrity before the digital age. title: NYC Ramadan Night Market
tagline: Celebrate Ramadan in the heart of Little Egypt with halal food, culture, and community.
description: A community-driven Ramadan night market on Steinway Street in Astoria with halal street food, Muslim-owned vendor stalls, live music and cultural performances. It’s family-friendly — kids can try new foods, watch performers, and browse modest fashion and crafts. Free to enter; proceeds support Malikah’s mutual aid fund.
description_source: Next week, parts of Steinway Street in Astoria will be transformed into an Egyptian-style Ramadan night market. It was created by Rana Abdelhamid, the executive director and founder of Malikah, a Queens-based anti-violence organization. She notes that in the U.S., Ramadan is often celebrated in private spaces because people shy away from visualizing their identity due to fear. In contrast, in Egypt, Ramadan is a public affair with markets and festivals. Sponsored by Malikah, the first NYC Ramadan Night Market brought together hundreds of attendees for food, music, and community. The event returns as a fundraiser for Malikah’s mutual aid fund, with all proceeds supporting local families.

title: Video Games: The Great Connector
tagline: Explore the role of video games in youth development
description: At The Long Island Museum in Stony Brook, Video Games: The Great Connector is an interactive exhibit with 10 hands-on gaming stations that show how games teach teamwork, problem-solving and social skills. Kids ages 6–17 can play through challenges, spot hidden design choices, and meet featured game designers. The exhibit highlights contributions from people of color to inspire students toward game careers.
description_source: Learn how video games are more than a mode of entertainment, and the important role digital games are playing in the lives of today’s youth. The exhibition showcases that video games are more than a mode of entertainment for today’s youth; they have become a means for developing personal and professional skills, such as teamwork, complex problem-solving, and building social networks. Throughout the exhibit, which features 10 fun, interactive gaming stations, visitors will play games, meet figures in game design, and discover the unseen design elements that contribute to their gaming experiences. The exhibition celebrates contributions from people of color, inspiring Black and Latinx students to consider careers in the gaming industry.

description: CAMP NYC is an indoor play space in Manhattan with themed rooms like Bluey’s House, a Slime Bar, and hands-on craft stations for kids ages 3–10. title: Staten Island Fencing Club Interactive Demonstration
tagline: Discover the thrill of swordplay!
description: Kids ages 5–10 get to try basic fencing moves with plastic swords in this hands-on demo by the Richmond County Fencing Club. Children practice balance, footwork, and coordination in a safe, guided setting. Free with Staten Island Children’s Museum admission.
description_source: Discover the thrill of swordplay at a fencing demonstration designed especially for kids! The Richmond County Fencing Club, formerly known as Staten Island Fencing Club, will lead an action-packed event for young minds to learn about the art of balance and coordination and to practice with plastic swords. Unleash the inner swashbuckler in your child.
